From 3d970eda003441f66551a91fda16478ac0711617 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Ankit Garg <nktgrg@google.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Dec 2025 10:29:45 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] gve: defer interrupt enabling until NAPI registration

Currently, interrupts are automatically enabled immediately upon
request. This allows interrupt to fire before the associated NAPI
context is fully initialized and cause failures like below:

[    0.946369] Call Trace:
[    0.946369]  <IRQ>
[    0.946369]  __napi_poll+0x2a/0x1e0
[    0.946369]  net_rx_action+0x2f9/0x3f0
[    0.946369]  handle_softirqs+0xd6/0x2c0
[    0.946369]  ? handle_edge_irq+0xc1/0x1b0
[    0.946369]  __irq_exit_rcu+0xc3/0xe0
[    0.946369]  common_interrupt+0x81/0xa0
[    0.946369]  </IRQ>
[    0.946369]  <TASK>
[    0.946369]  asm_common_interrupt+0x22/0x40
[    0.946369] RIP: 0010:pv_native_safe_halt+0xb/0x10

Use the `IRQF_NO_AUTOEN` flag when requesting interrupts to prevent auto
enablement and explicitly enable the interrupt in NAPI initialization
path (and disable it during NAPI teardown).

This ensures that interrupt lifecycle is strictly coupled with
readiness of NAPI context.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Fixes: 1dfc2e46117e ("gve: Refactor napi add and remove functions")
Signed-off-by: Ankit Garg <nktgrg@google.com>
Reviewed-by: Jordan Rhee <jordanrhee@google.com>
Reviewed-by: Joshua Washington <joshwash@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Harshitha Ramamurthy <hramamurthy@google.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20251219102945.2193617-1-hramamurthy@google.com
Signed-off-by: Paolo Abeni <pabeni@redhat.com>

diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/google/gve/gve_main.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/google/gve/gve_main.c
index a7a088a77f37..7eb64e1e4d85 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ethernet/google/gve/gve_main.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ethernet/google/gve/gve_main.c
@@ -558,7 +558,7 @@ static int gve_alloc_notify_blocks(struct gve_priv *priv)
 		block->priv = priv;
 		err = request_irq(priv->msix_vectors[msix_idx].vector,
 				  gve_is_gqi(priv) ? gve_intr : gve_intr_dqo,
-				  0, block->name, block);
+				  IRQF_NO_AUTOEN, block->name, block);
 		if (err) {
 			dev_err(&priv->pdev->dev,
 				"Failed to receive msix vector %d\n", i);

diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/google/gve/gve_utils.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/google/gve/gve_utils.c
index ace9b8698021..b53b7fcdcdaf 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ethernet/google/gve/gve_utils.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ethernet/google/gve/gve_utils.c
@@ -112,11 +112,13 @@ void gve_add_napi(struct gve_priv *priv, int ntfy_idx,
 
 	netif_napi_add_locked(priv->dev, &block->napi, gve_poll);
 	netif_napi_set_irq_locked(&block->napi, block->irq);
+	enable_irq(block->irq);
 }
 
 void gve_remove_napi(struct gve_priv *priv, int ntfy_idx)
 {
 	struct gve_notify_block *block = &priv->ntfy_blocks[ntfy_idx];
 
+	disable_irq(block->irq);
 	netif_napi_del_locked(&block->napi);
 }
--

## Summary of Modifications

### Modifications per file:

1. **`drivers/net/ethernet/google/gve/gve_main.c`**:
   - Changed the `request_irq()` call in `gve_alloc_notify_blocks()` to include the `IRQF_NO_AUTOEN` flag instead of `0`. This prevents the interrupt from being automatically enabled when requested.

2. **`drivers/net/ethernet/google/gve/gve_utils.c`**:
   - In `gve_add_napi()`: Added a call to `enable_irq(block->irq)` after the NAPI context is initialized and the IRQ is linked to it.
   - In `gve_remove_napi()`: Added a call to `disable_irq(block->irq)` before tearing down the NAPI context with `netif_napi_del_locked()`.

### Relationship between modifications:
The change in `gve_main.c` defers interrupt enabling by removing the automatic enablement that occurred at IRQ request time. The additions in `gve_utils.c` take over the responsibility of enabling and disabling the interrupt explicitly when the NAPI context is added or removed. This ensures the interrupt only fires after its associated NAPI context is fully initialized and ready to handle packets, and that the interrupt is disabled before the NAPI context is destroyed, preventing the race condition described in the bug report.

## Summary of Modifications

The patch fixes a race condition where interrupts could fire before the associated NAPI context is fully initialized. The changes ensure that interrupt enablement is deferred until after NAPI registration and disabled before NAPI teardown.

### Modifications in `gve_main.c`

- **`gve_alloc_notify_blocks`**: Changed the `request_irq` call to use the `IRQF_NO_AUTOEN` flag (instead of `0`). This prevents interrupts from being automatically enabled at request time, avoiding premature interrupt delivery.

### Modifications in `gve_utils.c`

- **`gve_add_napi`**: Added a call to `enable_irq(block->irq)` after `netif_napi_add_locked` and `netif_napi_set_irq_locked`. This explicitly enables the interrupt only after the NAPI instance is fully set up and ready to handle polling.

- **`gve_remove_napi`**: Added a call to `disable_irq(block->irq)` before `netif_napi_del_locked`. This ensures the interrupt is disabled before NAPI removal, preventing any spurious interrupts during teardown.

### Relationship Between Modifications

The change in `gve_main.c` disables automatic interrupt enablement at the IRQ registration stage. The two changes in `gve_utils.c` then explicitly manage the interrupt state in tandem with NAPI lifecycle: enabling the interrupt only after NAPI is added, and disabling it before NAPI is removed. Together, these three modifications tightly couple the interrupt lifecycle with NAPI readiness, preventing the race condition that caused crashes.

## Summary of Modifications

The patch fixes a race condition where interrupts could fire before their associated NAPI context is fully initialized, leading to crashes. It achieves this by deferring interrupt enablement until NAPI registration.

### Changes per file

**`drivers/net/ethernet/google/gve/gve_main.c`**
- In `gve_alloc_notify_blocks()`: Changed the `request_irq()` call from passing `0` (default flags, which enables the interrupt immediately) to `IRQF_NO_AUTOEN`. This prevents the interrupt from being automatically enabled at request time.

**`drivers/net/ethernet/google/gve/gve_utils.c`**
- In `gve_add_napi()`: Added `enable_irq(block->irq)` after calling `netif_napi_add_locked()` and `netif_napi_set_irq_locked()`, ensuring the interrupt is only enabled once the NAPI context is fully set up.
- In `gve_remove_napi()`: Added `disable_irq(block->irq)` before calling `netif_napi_del_locked()`, ensuring the interrupt is disabled before the NAPI context is torn down.

### Relationship between the modifications

The changes are complementary and form a complete lifecycle management for interrupts:

1. **Prevention of premature interrupts**: By using `IRQF_NO_AUTOEN` in `request_irq()`, the interrupt is never enabled automatically. This eliminates the window between interrupt request and NAPI registration where an interrupt could fire on an uninitialized NAPI context.

2. **Controlled enabling**: The interrupt is explicitly enabled only after the NAPI context has been added and its IRQ set, in `gve_add_napi()`. This couples the interrupt enablement with NAPI readiness.

3. **Controlled disabling**: The interrupt is explicitly disabled before the NAPI context is removed, in `gve_remove_napi()`. This prevents any stray interrupts from reaching a partially torn-down NAPI.

Together, these modifications ensure that the interrupt lifecycle is strictly aligned with the NAPI context lifecycle, eliminating the race condition that caused the reported kernel crash.
